title: Even moment coefficient gap
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,l\in\mathbb N$. Write $q_r$ for the sharp even-moment noise quantity at $r$. The even moment coefficient gap is $\binom{2r}{2l}q_r^{2l}\,\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{law}}[X(x)^{2l}]-\binom rl$.
caveat: The snippet uses the sharp even-moment noise quantity but does not define its meaning.
